The Internet Archive scan of the Norton printing is lending-only, and no author-posted draft was found. The companion chapter the record already cites, Deacon & Cashman (2013), "Teleology versus mechanism in biology: beyond self-organization", is identified below but was not reachable either and is not filed. |
| [LIT-530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-530.md) | What Is Life? The Physical Aspect of the Living Cell | Schrödinger (1944), Cambridge University Press. Lectures given at Trinity College Dublin in February 1943, published as a short book for the lay reader. It asks how events inside a living organism can be accounted for by physics and chemistry. It treats the gene as an "aperiodic crystal" carrying a code-script, defended through the Delbrück model, and in chapter 6 says an organism keeps its order by drawing "order from order" and by feeding on negative entropy from its surroundings. Unread: registered from the publisher's description and contents; the text itself was not reached. | Deferred — registered 2026-10-02 from the publisher's description, the Cambridge Core contents and chapter excerpts, and library catalogue records, not read: no lawful full text could be reached. Every Internet Archive scan of a Cambridge or Macmillan printing is lending-only, and the freely downloadable PDFs that turn up (course sites, personal uploads, Internet Archive "opensource" uploads) are unauthorized copies of the Canto edition, so I did not open them. Chapter 6, the negative-entropy chapter, is unread beyond the publisher's one-paragraph excerpt. |
| [LIT-532](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-532.md) | Inadequacy of entropy and entropy derivatives in characterizing the steady state | Landauer (1975), DOI-10.1103/PhysRevA.12.636. Per its abstract: in a bistable system the kinetics of transitions between the two locally stable states can be changed without changing the behaviour near either state, so no quantity that characterises only the vicinity of the states can determine which is more probable. Separately, even a monostable linear circuit's steady state need not be one of minimum entropy production. Unread: filed from the abstract. | Deferred — seeded 2026-10-02 from its abstract and Crossref metadata, not read: no lawful full text could be reached (Physical Review A, closed; Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex list no open copy). Filed because it is the classic objection to entropy-based characterisations of nonequilibrium steady states, Prigogine's minimum principle among them; it stays Deferred until a copy is supplied. |
| [LIT-534](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-534.md) | Order Out of Chaos: Man's New Dialogue with Nature | Prigogine & Stengers (1984), Bantam; based on their La nouvelle alliance. A book for general readers that sets the science of complexity and irreversibility against classical dynamics. By its contents: the rise and limits of Newtonian science and its philosophical reception (Diderot, Kant, Hegel, Bergson, Whitehead); thermodynamics from Carnot to Boltzmann's order principle; linear and far-from-equilibrium thermodynamics, bifurcations and order through fluctuations; and the rediscovery of time in physics. Unread: filed from catalogue records only. | Deferred — filed 2026-10-02 from library catalogue records and a partial contents note; no lawful full text was reachable (the book is in copyright, the Internet Archive scans of the Bantam and Flamingo printings are lending-only, HathiTrust is search-only), so it is not read and no NOTE is filed. It is the popular and philosophical statement of the programme whose technical core is the Nobel lecture ([LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md)); what it argues, beyond its contents, is not recorded here. |
| [LIT-536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-536.md) | Biological Autonomy: A Philosophical and Theoretical Enquiry | Moreno & Mossio (2015), Springer, History, Philosophy and Theory of the Life Sciences 12. The book argues that biology should revolve around autonomy, not only natural selection: organisms are organized systems that self-produce and self-maintain as integrated wholes, set their own goals and norms, and promote the conditions of their existence through interaction with their environment. Chapters treat constraints and organisational closure, emergence and inter-level causation, teleology and function, agency, evolution, organisms and levels of autonomy, and cognition. The monograph of the Brussels thermodynamic stability theory. By the Nobel lecture's citations, it treats local equilibrium (ch. II), the second-order excess entropy δ²S as a Lyapounov function near equilibrium (ch. V), and the excess-entropy-production criterion far from equilibrium, including convection (ch. VII). ACT reduced global inflexibility, lack of present-moment awareness, fusion, experiential avoidance, self-as-content and inaction, and increased committed action/values, flexibility/acceptance and defusion, against waitlist and active comparators. The paper that named the biopsychosocial model. | [LIT-552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-552.md) | Toward a Philosophical Structure for Psychiatry | Kendler (2005), American Journal of Psychiatry 162(3):433–440. Eight propositions for a philosophical frame for psychiatry, per the abstract: psychiatry is grounded in first-person experience; Cartesian substance dualism and epiphenomenalism are false; brain→mind and mind→brain causation are both real; psychiatric disorders are etiologically complex, with no more "spirochete-like" discoveries to come; explanatory pluralism beats monism, especially biological reductionism; and the goal is "patchy reductionism" and "piecemeal integration". A web search finds it only on a document-sharing site, which is not an author or institutional deposit.
